challenges.headline: Auto-create means auto-issue?
challenges.premise: The invoice should simply be created on signature, with no stated human control point.
challenges.alternative: Creating a draft invoice on signature, then letting a named person issue it, keeps the time saving (no manual data entry) while leaving a check before a legally numbered document exists.
challenges.consequence: An issued invoice carries legal numbering and VAT. If the amount or billing contact is wrong, you face credit notes and numbering gaps instead of a simple edit.
challenges.recommendation: Agree with Finance that the automation produces drafts first. Revisit auto-issue only after the draft output has proved reliable.

challenges.headline: "An invoice" per contract
challenges.premise: One signed contract yields one invoice, created at the moment of signature.
challenges.alternative: A contract can have milestones, recurring or partial billing. Invoicing at a billing-schedule date, or only the first scheduled invoice at signature, avoids hard-coding a single full-amount invoice that may not match the commercial terms.
challenges.consequence: Building the one-invoice case first and discovering schedules later turns a small trigger into a billing engine, and a billing-rule change then ripples across every invoice a contract emits.
challenges.recommendation: Collect a sample of recent signed contracts and classify how each is actually billed before estimating.

challenges.headline: Build before checking what exists
challenges.premise: A new automation must be built, as nothing in the request says the invoicing module or another tool lacks it.
challenges.alternative: The invoicing module is already built. If it, or an external billing tool, already supports triggered or recurring billing that is not switched on, configuring it could replace most of the build.
challenges.consequence: Building a parallel mechanism duplicates logic and creates two sources of billing truth.
challenges.recommendation: Have someone who knows the invoicing module and current billing practice confirm what exists before scoping the build.

opportunities.text: Build the contract-signed subscriber as a reusable, idempotent event-handling pattern that other downstream automations can share.

next_steps: Confirm what the invoicing module and any external tool already do for triggered or recurring billing, and how invoices are created today after signature.

Decide with Finance: draft versus issued, who reviews, and what happens when billing data is incomplete.

challenges.headline: Invoice at signature, automatically
challenges.premise: A signed contract should immediately yield an invoice, as though one contract meant one invoice due at that moment.
challenges.alternative: Generate a draft at signature that a billing owner validates and issues, or drive invoices from a billing schedule (start date, milestones, recurrence). This keeps signature as the trigger without making it the moment of legal issuance.
challenges.consequence: An issued invoice carries legal numbering and VAT and cannot simply be edited. Auto-issuing at signature risks wrong or premature invoices, credit notes, and gaps in the numbering sequence when a deal changes before it starts. A contract is also one-to-many with invoices, so a single document may be the wrong shape.
challenges.recommendation: Agree with Finance that the automatic output is a draft, and establish whether contracts bill once, in milestones or recurringly, before estimating.

challenges.headline: Is building this even needed?
challenges.premise: Invoice automation has to be built new, with no check on what the platform already offers.
challenges.alternative: If the invoicing module already has recurring or scheduled billing, or an accounting tool handles it, switching that on or wiring it to the signature event may cover most of the need.
challenges.consequence: Building a second billing path alongside an unused existing one duplicates logic that must then follow the same VAT and numbering rules.
challenges.recommendation: Inventory the current invoicing features and the as-is manual process before committing scope.

challenges.headline: Signature as the only trigger
challenges.premise: Signature happens once per contract, so one trigger is enough.
challenges.alternative: Treat amendments as separate billing events with their own rule (adjust, add, or do nothing), and decide explicitly how contracts already signed before go-live are handled.
challenges.consequence: Because an amendment re-opens signature, a naive subscriber can bill the same contract again, or silently skip a change in value.
challenges.recommendation: Define the no-duplicate rule and the amendment behaviour before building the subscriber.

Contracts signed before go-live being missed or double-billed during rollout.

opportunities.text: Build the signature subscriber as a reusable event-to-action hook with idempotency, so other downstream automation (notifications, onboarding) can use the same pattern.
Route notifications by client contact role (billing, HR, operational), reusing the existing Contact roles.
Generalise to a billing schedule tied to the contract, covering milestones and recurring invoices, once the single-invoice case is proven.

Specify the no-duplicate rule, amendment behaviour and treatment of already-signed contracts.
Then build the draft-generation subscriber for the simplest confirmed case, with origin link and notification, and test it on a pilot client.

challenges.headline: Issue directly, or create drafts?
challenges.premise: The request says 'an invoice is created', which reads as a finished invoice appearing the moment the contract is signed.
challenges.alternative: Creating the invoice as a draft that Finance reviews and issues keeps the automation's output editable. Issuing straight away would put it under legal numbering and VAT rules, where it can only be corrected by a credit note.
challenges.consequence: Auto-issued invoices built from incomplete or wrong contract data consume legal sequence numbers, may reach the client's billing contact, and can only be fixed through credit notes.
challenges.recommendation: Propose draft-first as the default and ask Finance whether any client truly needs automatic issue, and if so, whether that should be a later per-client option.

challenges.headline: One signature, one invoice?
challenges.premise: The request treats the signature as producing a single invoice.
challenges.alternative: Treat the signature as the point where a billing schedule is established (full amount, milestones or recurring), and generate only the invoice(s) due now, with later ones coming from the schedule's own dates.
challenges.consequence: Building 'one invoice per signature' first would have to be reworked as soon as a milestone, recurring or partially billed contract appears, and a billing-rule change would not reach the invoices already created.
challenges.recommendation: Get from Finance a breakdown of current contracts by billing pattern and build for the most common one first, keeping the data model ready for schedules.

challenges.headline: Is signature the right trigger?
challenges.premise: Signature is assumed to be the moment billing should start, and amendment signatures are not addressed.
challenges.alternative: Invoicing at the contract's start date or on a billing schedule avoids billing contracts that are cancelled or changed before they begin, and gives amendment signatures an explicit rule rather than leaving them to re-fire the trigger.
challenges.consequence: Signature-triggered invoicing multiplies credit-note handling when deals change before they start, and an amendment signature can bill a second time if nobody defines it.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance whether billing starts on signature or on a later date, and write down that an amendment signature creates no invoice unless a rule says otherwise.

complexity_reasons: the amount and billing-rule source is undefined and may vary by client
idempotency and amendment handling around the signature event
legal numbering and VAT constraints on any issued invoice
handling incomplete source data without losing the signature
briefs.cost_driver: defining where the invoice amount and billing rules come from
risks: Duplicate invoices if the signature event is re-delivered or an amendment is signed.
Gaps or misuse of the legal numbering sequence if invoices are issued automatically and later cancelled.
Contracts already signed before launch being swept into the automation at rollout.
Incomplete contract data (no amount, billing contact or VAT rate) silently producing wrong invoices or none at all.
Permissions on auto-created invoices are unspecified, and approval and permission rules are shared across modules, so a change may touch several screens.

opportunities.text: Make the contract-signature event a documented, reliable trigger with idempotent delivery that other automations can subscribe to.
Model a contract's billing schedule explicitly (full, milestone, recurring) so that future billing automation reuses it rather than adding one-off rules.
Route notifications by the client contact's role (billing contact) using the existing directory.

next_steps: Run a short session with Finance to settle the amount source, draft versus issued, and the most common billing pattern, and find out how invoices are created today.
Check whether the invoicing module already has an automation or billing-rule feature that is not switched on before scoping any build.
Define the rules for duplicates, amendments and incomplete data, plus acceptance scenarios, before estimating.
Build a first version that creates draft invoices for the most common billing pattern, with a traceable link to the contract, and pilot it on a limited set of clients.

decisions.tradeoff: Less flexibility than a dedicated tool, in exchange for a smaller build and a single place for invoice data.

decisions.decision: Contract signature is the event the automation listens to.
Automatically created invoices start as drafts, not issued.
decisions.why: Issued invoices fall under legal numbering and VAT rules and cannot be edited, while the source data is not yet known to be reliable.
decisions.alternative: Issue and send immediately on signature.
decisions.tradeoff: An extra review step, in exchange for much lower risk of wrong invoices and numbering gaps.
